lessons.title: How the NWSL works
lessons.objective: You can explain NWSL structure, the Shield and the playoffs.

payload.prompt: Which of these is true of the NWSL?

options.text: The bottom three clubs are relegated each year
There is no relegation, so the same clubs stay in the league
It is run by England's FA

explanation.correct: Right. The NWSL has no relegation. Clubs keep their place, and the title is decided in the playoffs.
explanation.incorrect: The NWSL is a closed league with no relegation. It is not run by England's FA.
explanation.sayThisLine: No relegation in the NWSL, so the clubs stay put.

payload.prompt: Match the NWSL trophy to what it rewards.

pairs.definition: Awarded to the team with the best record in the regular season, regardless of playoff results.
Decided in the playoffs; the winner is crowned champion after the postseason tournament.
All teams play the same number of matches; the Shield winner leads the table at the end.

explanation.summary: The Shield goes to the regular-season leader; the Championship is won in the playoffs, just like in MLS.
explanation.sayThisLine: You can win the Shield but lose in the playoffs.

payload.template: In the NWSL, the {{champion}} is decided in the playoffs after the regular season ends, so a hot team can win it all.

explanation.correct: Right. The Championship is won in the playoffs; it's not a given to the regular-season leader.
explanation.incorrect: The NWSL Championship is decided through a playoff tournament. The Shield leader has an advantage but has to win the playoffs to claim the title.

payload.prompt: Gotham won the 2025 NWSL Championship as the lowest seed ever to do it. True or false?

scene.alt: A playoff bracket with the lowest seed advancing to the final.

explanation.correct: True. Gotham beat the Washington Spirit 1-0 in the 2025 final, the lowest seed ever to win it. It shows how open the playoffs are.
explanation.incorrect: Gotham did win in 2025 as the lowest seed ever to lift the trophy, beating Washington 1-0. Anything can happen in a playoff.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: We won the Shield but lost in the playoffs. So frustrating.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: Her team finished first in the regular season but lost in the playoff tournament
Her team failed to qualify for the playoffs
Her team had the best regular-season record but didn't win the title

payload.translation: Her team had the best record all season and won the Supporters' Shield, but a different team won the Championship in the playoffs, so they didn't end up as overall champions.

followUps.line: Does that happen often in the NWSL?
followUps.why: Shows you know it's possible but noteworthy.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: It's okay to ask which team won the title if you don't know; that's a real question.

lessons.title: Why the boom is recent
lessons.objective: You can explain why the NWSL and women's football are booming now.

payload.prompt: The FA (England's football association) banned women's football from affiliated grounds for how long?

explanation.correct: Right. Fifty years of official suppression. England's FA did not lift the ban until 1971.
explanation.incorrect: England's FA banned women's football from its members' grounds from 1921 to 1971. That is fifty years of setbacks.
explanation.sayThisLine: The fifty-year ban killed women's football for decades in England.

payload.prompt: Match the milestone to its significance for women's football growth.

pairs.definition: Held in the USA, the final drew 90,000 fans; a cultural moment that showed women's football could draw crowds.
A professional league for women in the US, proving a market for women's football and creating stable careers.
Rising TV deals, attendance, investment and sponsorships for women's leagues globally since the 2010s.

explanation.summary: The 1999 World Cup proved the audience was there; the NWSL gave players a league; modern investment followed.
explanation.sayThisLine: The 1999 World Cup was the turning point.

payload.prompt: She says women's football is "new". How do you respond?

situation.narrative: A friend mentions that women's football has only just taken off.

facts.value: The FA banned women's football from its grounds
USA hosts a Women's World Cup with huge crowds

options.label: Agree, then mention the ban and how recent the investment is
options.consequence: She feels heard and you show you know the story: the game is old, the boom is recent.
considerations: The ban held the game back for fifty years
Investment and coverage are the recent part

options.label: Just nod and say "yeah, so new"
options.consequence: Friendly, but you miss the chance to share the real story behind the boom.
considerations: Adding one fact makes it a real conversation

options.label: Tell her she has it all wrong
options.consequence: She feels corrected instead of listened to, and the conversation stalls.
considerations: She is mostly right about the boom being recent
Corrections land better as curious additions

payload.expertNote: Fans who love the women's game like hearing that the sport is old but was held back. Adding context works better than correcting.
payload.sayThisLine: The game is old, it was held back for years, and the boom is recent.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: The atmosphere was unreal, the whole end sang for ninety minutes.

payload.question: Is she talking about the NWSL or men's football?

options.text: NWSL crowds can now create the kind of atmosphere you expect from big fixtures
Women's crowds are still always small and quiet
NWSL attendance and fan culture have grown dramatically
It must be men's football because women's doesn't draw

payload.translation: NWSL matches now draw big crowds and create real atmospheres. Women's football in the US has invested in itself and fans show up.

followUps.line: How many fans showed up to this match?
Is your team's home crowd always like this?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You can say you've noticed women's football crowds growing if you have.

payload.title: Women's football is here
payload.setting: She is excited about women's football investment and growth.

exchanges.theirMessage: The investment in women's football is finally real. Did you watch the NWSL this year?

replies.text: A bit, I've noticed the crowds are much bigger than they used to be. What matches stood out?
replies.theirResponse: Gotham's run to the title from eighth seed, that was wild.
replies.coachNote: Shows you see the growth and invites her insight.

replies.text: No, but I've heard there's more money in it now.
replies.coachNote: Honest and opens the door; not pretending to know more.

replies.text: Women's football isn't as good as men's anyway.
replies.coachNote: Never dismiss what she loves or reduce women's football.

payload.closingNote: She is proud of the NWSL's growth and wants to share it.
